Luminosity function (astronomy)

Words: 27
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
An astronomical luminosity function gives the number density of objects per luminosity interval, often also per comoving volume. Integrating luminosity times the function gives their luminosity density.

Astronomical magnitude

Words: 69 Articles: 3
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
Astronomical magnitude is a logarithmic measure of the brightness of an astronomical source; a smaller magnitude denotes a brighter source.

Apparent magnitude (m)

Words: 12
Astronomical magnitude OurBigBook.com
Apparent magnitude measures how bright an astronomical source appears to an observer.

Absolute magnitude (M)

Words: 22
Astronomical magnitude OurBigBook.com
Absolute magnitude is the apparent magnitude that an astronomical source would have at a conventional reference distance. It separates intrinsic luminosity from distance-dependent dimming.

Distance modulus (μ)

Words: 15
Astronomical magnitude OurBigBook.com
The distance modulus is the difference between apparent magnitude and absolute magnitude. For distance d in parsecs,
μ=m−M=5log10​(d/10pc).
(1)

Exoplanet

Words: 2k Articles: 69
Astrophysics OurBigBook.com
An exoplanet is a planet orbiting a star other than the Sun.

Exoplanet atmosphere

Words: 1k Articles: 54
Exoplanet OurBigBook.com
An exoplanet atmosphere controls the planet's spectrum, heat redistribution, chemistry, clouds, and atmospheric escape.

Radiative efficiency of black-hole accretion (η)

Words: 101 Articles: 2
Black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
The radiative efficiency is η=L/(M˙c2). For a zero-torque thin disk it is 1−EISCO​, the binding energy per unit rest mass released before matter crosses the innermost stable circular orbit.
Maximal radiative efficiency of black-hole accretion (ηmax​)
Words: 33
Radiative efficiency of black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
The maximal radiative efficiency is the available binding energy per unit accreted rest-mass energy when all energy released outside the capture boundary escapes as radiation. A relativistic zero-torque disk has ηmax​=1−EISCO​.
Innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO)
Words: 34
Radiative efficiency of black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
The innermost stable circular orbit is the smallest stable circular timelike orbit around a black hole. Its radius and orbital energy depend on black-hole spin and on whether the orbit is prograde or retrograde.

Bondi accretion

Words: 269 Articles: 10
Black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
Bondi accretion is steady spherical accretion from a uniform gas reservoir onto a compact gravitating object. In its adiabatic form, compression raises internal energy without providing the irreversible shear heating of a radiatively efficient disk.
Bondi–Hoyle accretion
Words: 44 Articles: 1
Bondi accretion OurBigBook.com
Bondi--Hoyle--Lyttleton accretion is gravitational capture by a compact object moving through a gas. In the pressureless supersonic limit, ballistic streamlines focus into a downstream wake.
Bondi--Hoyle--Lyttleton accretion rate (M˙BHL​)
Words: 19
Bondi–Hoyle accretion OurBigBook.com
In the ballistic supersonic limit, streamline collisions bind gas with impact parameter b<2GM/v∞2​, giving
M˙BHL​=v∞3​4πG2M2ρ∞​​.
(72)
Isothermal Bondi accretion
Words: 79 Articles: 3
Bondi accretion OurBigBook.com
Isothermal Bondi accretion has p=cs2​ρ with constant sound speed. Its regular transonic solution crosses the Bondi sonic point and approaches free fall near the accretor.

Words: 57 Articles: 2
Isothermal Bondi accretion OurBigBook.com
For inward speed u>0, steady spherical mass conservation and radial momentum balance give
(u−ucs2​​)drdu​=r2cs2​​−r2GM​.
(73)
Bondi sonic point (rs​)
Words: 41 Articles: 1
Isothermal Bondi equation OurBigBook.com
The isothermal Bondi sonic point is rs​=GM/(2cs2​), where the regular transonic solution has u=cs​.

Words: 25
Bondi sonic point OurBigBook.com
At the critical point, both the coefficient of du/dr and the remaining right-hand side of the Isothermal Bondi equation vanish, allowing a finite derivative through the sonic transition.

Words: 62 Articles: 1
Bondi accretion OurBigBook.com
The mass accretion rate is the mass entering an accretor per unit time. In a steady spherical flow, M˙=4πr2ρu is independent of radius.

Words: 36
Mass accretion rate OurBigBook.com
For a background gravitating density ρdm​=Ψ0​r−5/2, the potential is Φ=−16πGΨ0​r−1/2. A steady polytropic inflow has a regular sonic point only for 1<γ<9/7, and its accretion rate scales as M˙∝ρ0​G4Ψ04​c0−7​.
Free-fall speed (vff​)
Words: 16
Bondi accretion OurBigBook.com
The Newtonian free-fall speed from rest at infinity toward a point mass is vff​=2GM/r​.

For an adiabatic gas with γ=5/3, asymptotic density ρ0​, and sound speed vs0​ accreting onto a Newtonian point mass M, the largest globally subsonic steady rate is
M˙crit​=vs03​πρ0​(GM)2​.

Radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF)

Words: 298 Articles: 8
Black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
A radiatively inefficient accretion flow carries a substantial fraction of locally generated energy with the gas instead of radiating it before accretion. It can occur at low density because emission is weak or at high optical depth because photons are trapped.
Advection-dominated accretion flow (ADAF)
Words: 98 Articles: 2
Radiatively inefficient accretion flow OurBigBook.com
An advection-dominated accretion flow is a hot, geometrically thick, radiatively inefficient flow in which most dissipated energy remains in the gas and is carried inward rather than radiated locally.
Two-temperature accretion flow
Words: 69 Articles: 1
Advection-dominated accretion flow OurBigBook.com
A two-temperature accretion flow has ions and electrons at substantially different temperatures because their Coulomb equilibration time exceeds the inflow time. Ions can retain most viscous heat while electrons, which radiate more effectively, remain cooler.
Electron--proton thermal equilibration time (te−p​)
Words: 34
Two-temperature accretion flow OurBigBook.com
The electron--proton thermal equilibration time is the timescale on which Coulomb collisions exchange energy between electron and proton populations. Its inverse dependence on number density helps make dilute accretion flows two-temperature and radiatively inefficient.
Slim accretion disk
Words: 85 Articles: 2
Radiatively inefficient accretion flow OurBigBook.com
A slim accretion disk is an optically thick, moderately geometrically thick flow at a high accretion rate. Its inflow time can be shorter than its photon-diffusion time, so radial advection carries trapped radiation inward.
Photon trapping in an accretion flow
Words: 51 Articles: 1
Slim accretion disk OurBigBook.com
Photon trapping occurs when the radiative diffusion time across an optically thick flow exceeds its inward advection time. The trapped radiation is carried inward, reducing the emergent radiative efficiency.
Photon-trapping radius (rt​)
Words: 22
Photon trapping in an accretion flow OurBigBook.com
The photon-trapping radius is where the outward radiative diffusion time equals the inward inflow time. Radiation generated inside it is predominantly advected toward the accretor.
Luminous hot accretion flow (LHAF)
Words: 31
Radiatively inefficient accretion flow OurBigBook.com
A luminous hot accretion flow has radiative cooling greater than local viscous heating, so compressive inward advection supplies the difference. In the convention qadv​=q+−q−, it has qadv​<0.
Accretion-flow advection balance (qadv​=q+−q−)
Words: 43
Radiatively inefficient accretion flow OurBigBook.com
The accretion-flow advection balance compares local volumetric heating q+, radiative cooling q−, and energy transport with the gas. Positive qadv​ means advection removes locally generated heat; zero gives local radiative balance; negative means advection supplies heat that is radiated locally.

Eddington ratio (fEdd​)

Words: 80 Articles: 2
Black-hole accretion OurBigBook.com
The Eddington ratio is the luminosity divided by the Eddington luminosity. At fixed radiative efficiency it also measures the accretion rate relative to the Eddington rate.
Eddington accretion rate (M˙Edd​)
Words: 33
Eddington ratio OurBigBook.com
An Eddington accretion rate converts the Eddington luminosity into a mass supply rate using an adopted reference efficiency η0​: M˙Edd​=LEdd​/(η0​c2). The common choice η0​=0.1 gives M˙Edd​=10LEdd​/c2.
Salpeter time (tSal​)
Words: 21
Eddington ratio OurBigBook.com
The Salpeter time is the e-folding time for Eddington-limited black-hole growth. If tE​=σT​c/(4πGmp​), then tSal​=ηtE​/[(1−η)fEdd​].

Intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH)

Words: 19
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
An intermediate-mass black hole has a mass between stellar remnants and supermassive black holes, approximately 102--105M⊙​.

Supermassive black hole (SMBH)

Words: 466 Articles: 14
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
A supermassive black hole has a mass of roughly 106M⊙​ or more and commonly occupies the nucleus of a massive galaxy.

Black-hole--bulge mass relation

Words: 44
Supermassive black hole OurBigBook.com
The black-hole--bulge mass relation is the empirical correlation between a galaxy's central black-hole mass and the stellar mass of its spheroidal component. Locally, the black hole is typically of order 10−3--10−2 of the bulge mass, with substantial scatter and possible redshift evolution.

Active galactic nucleus (AGN)

Words: 368 Articles: 11
Supermassive black hole OurBigBook.com
An active galactic nucleus is a compact luminous galactic nucleus powered primarily by accretion onto a supermassive black hole.
Quasar
Words: 44 Articles: 1
Active galactic nucleus OurBigBook.com
A quasar is an extremely luminous active galactic nucleus whose compact central emission can be observed across cosmological distances.
Quasar light curve
Words: 25
Quasar OurBigBook.com
A quasar light curve records its measured brightness as a function of time. Intrinsic accretion variability, measurement noise, and gravitational lensing can all contribute structure.
Active-galactic-nucleus feedback (AGN feedback)
Words: 305 Articles: 8
Active galactic nucleus OurBigBook.com
Active-galactic-nucleus feedback transfers radiative or mechanical energy and momentum from black-hole accretion to surrounding galactic gas.
Active-galactic-nucleus wind bubble (AGN wind bubble)
Words: 142 Articles: 3
Active-galactic-nucleus feedback OurBigBook.com
An active-galactic-nucleus wind bubble forms when a fast nuclear wind shocks against galactic gas. From inside outward it contains free wind, a reverse shock, shocked wind, a contact discontinuity, a swept-up shocked shell, a forward shock, and undisturbed interstellar gas.
Momentum-driven outflow
Words: 39
Active-galactic-nucleus wind bubble OurBigBook.com
An outflow is momentum driven when shocked driving material cools rapidly, so it cannot retain enough thermal energy to inflate a pressure-supported bubble. The swept shell then receives approximately the direct wind momentum flux, often of order L/c.
Energy-driven outflow
Words: 63 Articles: 1
Active-galactic-nucleus wind bubble OurBigBook.com
An outflow is energy driven when cooling of the shocked wind is slow. Its hot bubble stores mechanical energy and expands by pressure work on the swept-up shell.
Momentum boost
Words: 35
Energy-driven outflow OurBigBook.com
A momentum boost is a shell momentum flux exceeding the direct input momentum flux. An energy-conserving wind of speed vw​ driving a shell of speed vs​≪vw​ can give p˙​s​/(L/c) of order vw​/(2vs​).
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell
Words: 147 Articles: 3
Active-galactic-nucleus feedback OurBigBook.com
A dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell is swept up when ultraviolet radiation from an active nucleus is absorbed by dust and reradiated in the infrared. Single scattering supplies up to roughly L/c of momentum flux, while trapped infrared photons can enhance it by the infrared optical depth.
Critical luminosity of a dusty shell (Lcrit​)
Words: 36
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
The critical luminosity of a dusty shell is the luminosity at which radiation pressure balances gravity. For shell mass Ms​, enclosed gravitating mass M, and ultraviolet and infrared optical depths,
Lcrit​=r2(1+τIR​−e−τUV​)GcMMs​​.
(75)

Words: 38
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
For a spherical swept shell of mass Ms​(R), radial speed R˙, driving force Fd​, and enclosed gravitating mass M(<R),
dtd​[Ms​(R)R˙]=Fd​−R2GMs​(R)M(<R)​.
(76)
The derivative includes momentum needed to accelerate newly swept ambient mass.
Dust transparency radius (Rτ​)
Words: 28
Dusty radiation-pressure-driven shell OurBigBook.com
The dust transparency radius is where a swept shell's ultraviolet optical depth equals one. For a gas fraction fg​ in a singular isothermal sphere, Rτ​=κUV​fg​σ2/(2πG).

Soltan argument

Words: 33
Supermassive black hole OurBigBook.com
The Soltan argument compares the cosmological energy density radiated by active galactic nuclei with the present mass density in supermassive black holes. Their ratio constrains the mass-weighted mean radiative efficiency of black-hole growth.

Tidal disruption event (TDE)

Words: 101 Articles: 2
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
A tidal disruption event occurs when a star passes close enough to a black hole that differential gravity tears it apart outside the capture boundary, producing returning debris and often a luminous flare.

Tidal disruption radius (rt​)

Words: 32
Tidal disruption event OurBigBook.com
For a star of mass M∗​ and radius R∗​ near a black hole of mass MBH​, the Newtonian tidal disruption radius is rt​≃R∗​(2MBH​/M∗​)1/3 under a peak-to-center tidal-acceleration convention.

Hills mass

Words: 36
Tidal disruption event OurBigBook.com
The Hills mass is the black-hole mass above which a given star crosses the capture boundary before being tidally disrupted. For a Schwarzschild capture radius 2GMBH​/c2, it is c3R∗3/2​/(2G3/2M∗1/2​) with the corresponding tidal-radius convention.

Black-hole seed

Words: 113 Articles: 3
Astrophysical black hole OurBigBook.com
A black-hole seed is an early black hole from which a later massive black hole can grow by accretion and mergers.

Population III remnant black-hole seed

Words: 30
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A Population III remnant seed forms when a massive metal-free star collapses, typically leaving a light seed of order 10--102M⊙​ depending on stellar mass loss and pair-instability effects.

Runaway stellar-collision black-hole seed

Words: 33
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A runaway stellar-collision seed forms when mass segregation and repeated mergers in a dense young cluster create a very massive star that collapses to a black hole of roughly 102--104M⊙​.

Direct-collapse black-hole seed (DCBH seed)

Words: 29
Black-hole seed OurBigBook.com
A direct-collapse black-hole seed forms when rapidly inflowing primordial gas avoids fragmentation, builds a supermassive star or quasistar, and collapses to a seed of roughly 104--106M⊙​.
